title: Nail clippers
prompt: a large nail clippers holding a strip of imitation nail on a table with three buttons: “Fold” opens the operating handle; “Press” squeezes the jaws through the strip; “Release” lets the jaws spring apart; see-through reveals the second-class handle pressing the paired third-class cutting levers
blurb: An enlarged nail clipper cuts an imitation nail strip to reveal its compound lever action.

identity.note: Levers / Multiple levers / Nail clippers, page 23. A second-class operating handle presses paired third-class cutting blades.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct compound arrangement versus scissors, pliers and tweezers. Retain the operating handle and flexible cutting blades rather than making scissors with clipper styling.

prompt.note: Faithful. Fold stages the operating handle, Press cuts the imitation strip, and Release lets elastic blades reopen. Keep handle pivot and blade fulcrum separate and identify both stages. The strip is a teaching substitute for a nail.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

truthNotes: Second-class operating handle loads paired third-class spring blades.
Post pulls the lower blade; cam toe presses the upper blade; joined heel is the separate blade fulcrum.
The spring blades reopen without an added coil spring.
Table, support block and imitation-nail specimen are teaching adaptations.
Fold simplifies full storage flip-and-swivel to lifting the handle.
The detached tip exits sideways before falling to the table.
Release does not repair the specimen; reload provides a fresh specimen.
1988 inaccessible and unverified; no edition-union claim.

constructionReference.use: Representative resilient jaws, pull post, cross-bar and operating cam lever, not an assertion of the book drawing exact manufacture.
